intervals.label: e+e- collider operation (DORIS, DORIS II, DORIS III)
intervals.locator: DORIS history page, 1974 entry; end from the 1993 entry
intervals.note: Year-precision start (the page gives no month); end is the year the page says DORIS became a dedicated synchrotron-radiation source.
intervals.quote: The storage ring DORIS is build as an electron-positron collider for high energy physics.

intervals.label: DORIS (two rings)
intervals.note: Original double-ring machine (DOppel-RIng-Speicher), initially up to 3 GeV per beam; end = the 1982 upgrade to DORIS II.
intervals.quote: Towards the end of 1974, the two detectors PLUTO and DASP were placed in their respective collision points.

beam_energy.note: Initial energy; raised to close to 5 GeV per beam before the 1982 upgrade.
beam_energy.quote: initially stored electrons and positrons with energies of up to 3 GeV

intervals.label: DORIS II (single ring)
intervals.note: Single-ring operation at up to 5.6 GeV per beam; hosted ARGUS and Crystal Ball. End = the 1991 upgrade to DORIS III.
intervals.quote: DORIS was upgraded in 1982 to reemerge as DORIS II

beam_energy.note: Beam energy in the DORIS II era.
beam_energy.quote: The higher energies of 5.6 GeV per beam

intervals.label: DORIS III (ARGUS running)
intervals.note: DORIS III modified one long straight section for synchrotron-radiation insertion devices; the other straight section kept ARGUS running until 1993.
intervals.quote: In the second straight the very successful ARGUS detector is operating until 1993 for high energy physics.

intervals.label: collider operation ended
intervals.note: Particle-physics running ended; DORIS then served only as a synchrotron-radiation source (until 2012 per Ziemann, "German Beams"). This record covers the collider only.
intervals.quote: DORIS is running as a dedicated source for synchrotron radiation.

name: Doppel-Ring-Speicher
notes: End of collider running: the DESY DORIS page says ARGUS operated "until 1993"; other sources give end of data taking in 1992. The record follows the DESY page (1993) and marks it approximate.

summary.plain: DESY's first electron-positron collider, in Hamburg, running from 1974. It confirmed the charm quark's bound states, produced Upsilon mesons after its 1982 upgrade, and hosted ARGUS, which first saw B-meson mixing in 1987, and Crystal Ball.
summary.technical: DORIS e⁺e⁻ storage ring, 288 m circumference; two rings up to 3 GeV per beam from 1974 (PLUTO, DASP), single-ring DORIS II from 1982 at up to 5.6 GeV per beam (ARGUS, Crystal Ball), DORIS III from 1991; high-energy-physics running ended 1993, after which it served only as a synchrotron-radiation source.
